scenes.headline: How NVIDIA Model Optimizer turns a model into FP4
scenes.sub: Read from the source code, then from the bytes of DeepSeek-R1-FP4.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Crouton! NVIDIA makes its own four-bit checkpoints with this library. Here's how it quantizes a model, and what lands on disk.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Swap every linear layer for one that carries quantizers, calibrate their scales on real data, then export the scales beside the packed weights.
scenes.say: Swap in quantizers, calibrate their scales on real data, and export the scales beside the packed weights.

steps.say: Every linear layer becomes a quantized twin with three quantizers: input, weight and output.
An ordered list of patterns switches them on or off. The output head and the routers stay off.
Calibration data flows through, and each quantizer records the largest value it must represent.
Export packs the weights, writes the scales beside them, and tags the config for vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT.

scenes.title: NVFP4: two scales and a nibble
scenes.text: w = e2m1 x s_block x s_tensor
scenes.say: Each weight is a code times two scales.

parts.note: 4-bit code: eight magnitudes from 0 to 6, plus sign
parts.say: A four-bit code: eight magnitudes up to six, plus a sign.
An eight-bit scale for every sixteen weights. The default sends each block's largest value to six.
And one thirty-two-bit scale covers the whole tensor.

scenes.title: Four ways to pick a scale
scenes.say: Four ways to choose that block scale.

items.text: Max: the largest value maps to 6
items.say: Max: the largest value maps to six.
The activation-aware search tries eleven exponents and keeps the least output error.
The squared-error sweep tries all one hundred twenty-six codes per block.

items.text: Local Hessian: weight error by inputs
items.say: Local Hessian weighs that error by the block's own inputs.

steps.say: NVIDIA's own plot: max scaling piles values into a bump around six.
Searched scales pull that mass onto the grid points instead.

scenes.title: DeepSeek-R1 on disk
scenes.say: From the headers: six hundred eighty-eight point six gigabytes in FP8, and four hundred twenty-three point six in four-bit.

scenes.text: NVFP4 costs 4.5 bits a weight; a checkpoint costs whatever you leave in BF16.

recap: 4-bit codes, FP8 block scales, FP32 tensor scale
